third_setting.finding: the learning rate was the whole problem. At 50 rows and batch 16, 10000 steps at TFM-Playground's default lr 1e-4 give R2 -0.046 on a plain linear task with 35 context rows; the same run at 3e-4 gives +0.821, against +0.463 for their released regressor. Both took 11 minutes. The two earlier settings, which learned nothing, used 1e-4
third_setting.tables: 50 rows, 1 to 3 features, context 20 to 39, the size the released regressor was trained at
third_setting.budget: 10000 steps of 16 tables at lr 3e-4, no gradient checkpointing, 100 buckets, about 11 minutes and 240 tables/s per run, so the whole 2 x 2 on two seeds fits in 1.5 hours
third_setting.evaluation: N_TRAIN=35, far below the hundreds of rows the thesis measures: this tests the mechanism, not the size of the effect
third_setting.probes_kept: nanoTabPFN-A0B0-s21 (batch 4, lr 1e-4, 25000 steps), s31 (lr 1e-4) and s32 (lr 3e-4), the pair that isolated the learning rate
third_setting.first_try_seeds_41_42: 3-feature dumps, lr 3e-4 without warmup. Half the runs blew up: A0B1-s41 ended at NaN, A0B1-s42 at 7.28, A1B0-s41 at 12.90, and their R2 on the linear task is about -0.05, while A0B0-s41 reached +0.621, A0B0-s42 +0.848 and A1B1-s41 +0.830. Their gate could not be read at all: the generator of this repo draws 5 features and the adapter refused every cell against a pre-training maximum of 3, which is the refusal it was written for. Those 640 rows were dropped from the result file before the next gate, since the key would otherwise count them as measured
third_setting.warmup_probe: with 1000 warmup steps at 3e-4, A1B0 is stable (loss 1.80, 1.12, 0.50 at steps 2000, 4000, 6000) and A0B1 is not (1.68, 1.54, 2.64): the robust encoding is the fragile arm, plausibly because the IQR of a 20 to 39 row context is noisy

later_local_attempts.pattern: the only models that learned had 3 features on 35-row contexts, about 12 rows per feature; with 8 features, 4.4 rows per feature, none did. The generator of this repo draws 5 features, so the setting that learns cannot be evaluated
later_local_attempts.conclusion: 2026-09-16 13:10: no local setting at a usable table size produced a model that learns; the question moves to a Colab GPU with bf16 (run/colab_setup.sh, run/prior_pretraining_colab.sh), gated by experiments/h3_repair/prior_pretraining_check.py
later_local_attempts.colab: the Colab plan on this account offers CPU, T4 and a TPU; H100, A100, L4 and G4 need Colab Pro+. A T4 is Turing like the RTX 2060, without real bf16
later_local_attempts.seed_72_fp32: to separate fp16 from the recipe: 256-row tables, fp32 (--amp none), checkpointing, batch 8, lr 3e-4, no warmup, 1000 buckets, 2026-09-16 13:51 to 15:23, 11582 steps, 92656 tables, 17.2 tables/s at 1074 MB. The loss stayed at 1.40 to 1.49 from step 200 to the end, with one spike to 111 at step 5000; linear-task R2 -0.010, held-out prior R2 -0.007 and positive in 0 of 200, NLL gain over the context marginal 0.049 nats. DID NOT LEARN. fp16 is not the cause: at 256 rows the loss never leaves the level of the marginal, where at 50 rows and 3 features the same learning rate took it from 1.59 to 1.22 in 10000 steps

second_setting.why: the first setting failed its own gate and the model ignores x. On 200 held-out prior tables, A0B0-s1 beats a head told only the context marginal by 0.20 nats in 156 of 200 tables, but the R2 of its predicted median is -0.006 and positive in 6 of 200: after 56000 tables of 1024 rows it predicts nearly a constant. Rows cost quadratically in the attention between datapoints, so the second setting buys tables with rows

why_the_models_do_not_learn.measured: on a plain linear task (y = 2 x0 - x1 + noise, 200 context rows, 5 seeds) read through the same adapter: the released nanoTabPFN regressor gets R2 +0.62, A0B0-s1 -0.010, A0B0-s11 -0.017
why_the_models_do_not_learn.reading: the adapter is not the problem; the two runs here never learned to predict a conditional median, in sample as well as out
why_the_models_do_not_learn.hypothesis: optimiser steps, not tables. TFM-Playground's pretrain_regression.py defaults to 100 steps x 10000 epochs at batch 1, a million updates on 50-row tables; these runs made 7000 and 10000 updates. The next test follows their recipe: 50-row, 3-feature tables, small batch, many steps

recipe_test.dumps: 4 shards of 25000 tables at 50 rows and 1 to 3 features, context 20 to 39, seeds 6026 to 6029, .cache/tfmp/dumps/tiny_s60*.h5
recipe_test.nanoTabPFN-A0B0-s21: 2026-09-16 05:10 to 05:56, 24980 steps at batch 4, 100 buckets, loss 1.59 to 1.32; R2 on the linear task with 35 context rows -0.042, where the released regressor gets +0.463 (+0.446 at 40 rows). 25000 steps is 2.5% of their recipe
recipe_test.what_limits_the_steps: not the data path: preloading all 100000 tables into memory (0.07 GB) left the rate at 39 tables/s. The step itself is the cost. Without gradient checkpointing, which recomputes the forward pass and is pointless at 50 rows, the rate is 15.3 steps/s at batch 4 and 14.5 at batch 16, so the step rate is fixed by launch overhead (about 65 ms) and a larger batch is free data. Three hours buy about 160000 steps, 16% of their recipe

budget.target_clip_why: decided 2026-09-15 after the first A0B1 run: on shard 2026 the robust scale is below 0.01 sd in 2.68% of contexts, encoded targets reach 2.2e9, fp16 gives NaN. Share of contexts the cap touches (first 5000 tables): A0B0 0%, A0B1 0.70%, A1B0 0%, A1B1 2.60%; a cap at 100 would have touched 47.7% of A1B1 contexts and acted as a context repair
budget.why_steps_not_hours: every arm gets the same optimiser steps and the same tables in the same order; wall time is recorded per run
